paragraphs: He is mentioned in Ketubot 75a. He used to teach a baraita, and Rav Acha son of Rava and Rav Ashi examined and analyzed the words of the baraita that he brought.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The separately read Davidson Ketubot 75a passage explicitly has תני רבי נתן ביראה and the Acha-son-of-Rava/Ashi discussion, supporting Rabbi for this exact reciter. It does not establish a Tannaitic era or identify him with another Natan. עה. is 75a by convention; machine comma differs from the supplied period.

Supplied וטרו differs from machine ומרו; examined and analyzed follows the שקלו וטרו idiom across the line break. Full רב stays Rav for Acha and Ashi; Rava is an unprefixed name, without an additional father title.
